entities.summary: Gaius Caecina Largus (b. 50 BCE, Volterra) was a Roman military commander and civil administrator of the Classical era, known for his military leadership and administrative expertise. He played a significant role in the Roman Empire's expansion and governance, particularly in the region of Etruria. Largus's career spanned several decades, during which he served under various Roman governors and participated in numerous military campaigns, including the campaigns of Julius Caesar and Augustus. He was also involved in the administration of the Roman province of Etruria, overseeing the collection of taxes and the construction of public works projects. Largus's legacy extends beyond his military and administrative accomplishments, as he was also a patron of the arts and a supporter of the Roman Olympic Games. His contributions to the Roman Empire's military and administrative structures had a lasting impact on the development of Western civilization, shaping the course of Roman history and leaving a lasting legacy in the fields of politics, law, and governance. The city of Volterra, where Largus was born, remains a testament to his enduring influence on the region's history and culture. As a prominent figure of the Classical era, Gaius Caecina Largus's name continues to be remembered and studied by historians and scholars today, providing valuable insights into the complexities of Roman politics, society, and culture.
